Due dates

Wisconsin default (s. 74.11(2), Wis. Stats., statute page opened): real estate tax payable in full by January 31, or in 2 equal installments Jan 31 and Jul 31 (municipalities may offer more installments by ordinance). Milwaukee treasurer page references a January 31 first installment; online payment portal: https://cityofmilwaukeewi.tylerportico.com/navigator/public/selections/navigator. See the official page.

Challenging your assessment

Wisconsin rule (DOR BOR page opened): give the BOR clerk written or oral notice of intent to object at least 48 hours before the first BOR meeting, then file Objection Form PA-115A within the first two hours of the first meeting; the BOR may waive the 48-hour notice for good cause. City page (opened): Board of Review is an independent citizen board appointed by the Mayor and confirmed by the Common Council; postponements to the Clerk at least 2 business days before the hearing. Assessor page (op. See the official page.

We could not confirm the current Milwaukee rate on an opened page, so we do not state one.

  • Milwaukee city is in Milwaukee County (Census also lists 0-population parts in Washington and Waukesha counties).

Milwaukee by the numbers

Milwaukee has roughly 569,756 residents in the Census Bureau's 2019-2023 survey, and ranks number 1 by population among the 35 Wisconsin places in this guide. Owner-occupied homes have a median value of $172,000 here, which is 25% below the middle figure for the 35 Wisconsin places. About 59% of households rent, so 41% own; the Wisconsin median for these places is 60% owner-occupied. Homes here were typically built in 1952, so the median house is about 71 years old. These numbers describe Milwaukee as a whole, so a given street can sit well above or below them.
